title: Quantum-interference-driven orbital density wave and high-temperature superconductivity in trilayer nickelates
abstract: Intertwined charge-density-wave (CDW) and spin-density-wave (SDW) orders are a hallmark of high-temperature superconducting multilayer nickelates. In trilayer La4Ni3O_{10}, charge correlations develop at temperatures above the onset of long-range spin order, and the characteristic ordering wavevectors satisfy $Q_{cdw} \approx 2Q_{sdw}$. Here, using a density-wave equation with vertex corrections, we show that quantum interference between short-range SDW fluctuations at $q \approx Q_{sdw}$ on the outer NiO2 layers generates an inter-outer-layer bond order at $Q_{cdw} \approx 2 Q_{sdw}$. This bond order induces a pronounced inner-layer-centered orbital order, with antiphase modulations of the Ni $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ and $d_{x^2-y^2}$ occupations, producing strong orbital polarization but only weak total charge modulation. This intertwined bond-and-orbital order accounts for the layer-selective electronic reconstruction inferred from NMR/NQR and is consistent with Raman spectroscopy and scanning tunnelling microscopy measurements. The same orbital and spin fluctuations also cooperate to stabilize $s_{\pm}$-wave superconductivity through $M_z$ mirror-parity selection rules. Our results provide a unified microscopic framework for intertwined density-wave order and high-Tc superconductivity in multilayer nickelates.
summary: This theoretical study develops a unified framework for understanding high-Tc superconductivity in nickelates by showing that intertwined CDW and SDW orders are key. The mechanism involves quantum interference between spin fluctuations creating an orbital bond order, which in turn stabilizes the $s_{\pm}$-wave superconducting state. The work uses advanced many-body techniques to link structural order to superconducting pairing.
main_problem: The paper aims to microscopically understand the origin of intertwined charge-density-wave (CDW) and spin-density-wave (SDW) orders, and how this interplay drives high-temperature superconductivity in multilayer nickelates.
main_result: Quantum interference between short-range SDW fluctuations generates an inter-outer-layer bond order, which induces an inner-layer orbital order. This intertwined order stabilizes $s_{\pm}$-wave superconductivity.
method: The study employs a density-wave equation incorporating vertex corrections for CDW instability and uses the Bethe-Salpeter equation approach to calculate the superconducting pairing interaction.
model_or_system: The system is trilayer $	ext{La}_4	ext{Ni}_3	ext{O}_{10}$, modeled using a six-band approach focusing on the $	ext{Ni}$ $e_g$ orbitals. Electronic correlations are treated within the fluctuation-exchange (FLEX) approximation.
key_observables: CDW and SDW ordering wavevectors ($	ext{Q}_{	ext{cdw}}, 	ext{Q}_{	ext{sdw}}$), layer-selective orbital polarization, and the superconducting pairing symmetry ($s_{\pm}$-wave).
important_parameters: The relationship $	ext{Q}_{	ext{cdw}} \approx 2	ext{Q}_{	ext{sdw}}$ is central; the analysis also examines the role of the $\gamma$ pocket and the strength of spin fluctuations ($\alpha_S$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on treating quantum interference via vertex corrections (Aslamazov-Larkin terms) and uses approximations in the superconducting gap calculation (e.g., restricted energy cutoff $\Lambda=0.3$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the trilayer structure and band theory, the enhancement of CDW instability via quantum interference, the resulting orbital-resolved density modulations, and the diagrammatic representation of the pairing interaction components.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical context (CDW/SDW in nickelates), then detailing the theoretical framework (DW equation with vertex corrections), demonstrating the mechanism (quantum interference leading to bond/orbital order), and finally linking this order to the superconducting pairing mechanism.
why_interesting: While focused on strongly correlated materials, the use of fluctuation-driven instabilities and the explicit calculation of pairing interactions based on competing orders provides a rich theoretical framework applicable to understanding emergent quantum phases in many-body systems.

The d3z2−r2 (dx2−y2) orbital weight is expressed by red (green) color. Solid and dashed lines denote the Mz = +1 and −1 sectors, respectively. (c) Fermi surfaces with the d3z2−r2 and dx2−y2 orbital weights. Q1 and Q2 denote the characteristic nesting wavevectors. Inset: Dependence of the γ band near the M point on ∆E.

(b) Representative quantum-interference process in which two paramagnons generate charge and orbital fluctuations. The solid lines represent electronic Green functions. (b) Corresponding U dependences at T = 0.005. (c) and (d) Same as (a) and (b), respectively, but for ∆E = 0.1.

Orbital-density-wave and spin-density-wave structures: (a) Schematic representation of the linear-response process relating the microscopic DW form factor to the induced local density modulation. (b) Orbital-resolved density mod- ulations induced by the leading CDW form factor. The two Ni eg occupations modulate predominantly in antiphase, with particularly large amplitudes on the IL. FIG. 5. Cooperative superconducting pairing mediated by CDW and SDW fluctuations: (a) Schematic illustration of the Mz-parity selection rules for pairing interactions. CDW fluctuations mainly mediate attraction between Fermi pockets with the same Mz parity, whereas SDW fluctuations mediate repulsion between pockets with opposite parity. Red and blue indicate opposite signs of the s±-wave gap. Solid and dashed lines denote the Mz = +1 and −1 sectors, respectively.
